setting: You both live in Newcastle upon Tyne, in a rented flat in Jesmond, and have been together for six years. You're planning a weekend in Edinburgh this Saturday and need to choose between driving and taking the train. You both know the direct train from Newcastle takes about an hour and a half, that driving takes around two hours without traffic, and that parking in central Edinburgh is expensive.

Gemma.knows: You know Dan is your partner of six years, and you live together in his and your flat in Jesmond. You know he's careful with money and likes to have a plan before a trip.
Gemma.like: You're practical and organised, with a dry sense of humour that comes out most when you're tired.
Gemma.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when a decision needs an answer, since your days are busy at school.

Dan.knows: You know Gemma is your partner of six years, and you share your flat in Jesmond with her. You know she likes to check the details before committing to anything.
Dan.like: You're relaxed and easygoing, though you like to know the practical side of things before you say yes.
Dan.texts: You message in this chat mostly when you have something to add, and otherwise you wait to see what Gemma thinks.

private_lines.Gemma: You live in Jesmond, Newcastle, and work as a primary school teacher at a school a short walk from home. You share the flat with Dan, and your days start early with a run or a walk before work. You usually get home by half four, cook something simple, and spend evenings reading or watching television with Dan.
private_lines.Dan: You live in Jesmond, Newcastle, and work as an IT support engineer for a logistics firm in Gateshead, mostly from the office with a couple of days at home. You live with Gemma, and your days follow a steady routine of commuting, lunch at your desk, and a gym session two or three evenings a week. You usually head home around half five and spend the rest of the evening on the sofa with Gemma.

situation: A couple deciding whether to drive or take the train to Edinburgh on Saturday.
topic: What time is the last direct train from Edinburgh Waverley to London King's Cross on a Saturday?

text: what time is the last direct train from edinburgh waverley to london kings cross on a saturday
morning. no idea off the top of my head, I'd guess around 6 or 7 but check it
checking
last one's 18:00 on sats I think? the 18:30 might be sunday only, can't tell from the page
and i'm not doing a train at 6 if we're in town friday night, that's just silly
ok so we'd want to be back on it by 5 at the latest. that's fine if we're doing the day
driving would give us more flexibility on the way back though
home. hungry. can you sort the tuesday bin thing before you go to the gym
yep, on it
bins are out
thank you
parking in the castle area is £28 for the day on one of the sites i looked at. that's before we've even got there
yeah that's bad. there's a park and ride at the edge of the city though, might be worth checking
ingliston I think
ok i'll look at that tomorrow. i'm wiped
go to bed then. I'll sort dinner
goodnight
night
ok ingliston is £9 a day for park and ride which is fine. but if we drive the whole thing is roughly 2 hours each way and the train is 1h30 so
that's not that different though. the train's 1h30 door to door but we'd still need to get to the station and from waverley to wherever we're staying
and it's £60 return each for the train if we book now
£60 each is not what i saw. i saw £41 for the 08:02
that's the off peak one. the 08:02 is off peak but it's after 9 that's cheaper. i'm not sure which one i saw
can you just check the actual fare then
ok so it's £46 each for the 09:30 with the railcard. 8:02 is £41 with the railcard
so the train's probably £82 for both of us, driving is petrol plus £9 each for ingliston plus the hotel might have parking
does the hotel have parking
don't know yet. I'll check

yeah the Premier Inn by Haymarket. I'm not sure that's walkable to the castle
it's about 25 mins I think. fine
hotel says parking is £14 a night. so driving is more than I thought
right so ingliston 9 each, petrol maybe 25, hotel 14 for the night. that's still less than the train
yeah but add the time. and the drive back could be bad on a saturday evening
we're not coming back saturday night though, we said sunday
oh yeah. so we don't care about the saturday return. so we're not doing the day trip?
we talked about the day but then you said the hotel was booked. i'm confused now
sorry I think i got muddled. I booked the hotel for friday and saturday night, so we'd be there two nights
ok so we're not doing a day trip at all
i don't think so, unless you want to
i'm not sure i want to drive for 2 hours each way for a dinner and a castle
fair. the train's the easy option. we could just book the 09:30 on Friday and the Sunday return, I'll do it tomorrow if you're happy
go on then

nice. night
